metadata.note: The Virginian Railway, H. H. Rogers's coal road from the West Virginia Smokeless fields to Hampton Roads, as a passenger railroad: Norfolk - Victoria from 17 Jun 1907, through Norfolk - Roanoke - Princeton - Mullens - Deepwater from 1909, over the NYC to Charleston 1931-1951, and the Winding Gulf branch locals to 1940; the last train ran Norfolk - Roanoke on 29 Jan 1956, nearly four years before the 1 Dec 1959 N&W merger, so no Rule 4 split arises from that merger. The predecessor Deepwater Railway ran trains in its own name in 1906 - early 1907 and is drawn as a separate company in its own colour. Each main-line section is its own feature because its end year differs. Geometry is real OpenStreetMap trace (see each feature's geometry_quality); the Charleston leg is drawn on the NYC track the Virginian used by trackage rights, and 17.4 mi along the New River are drawn on the parallel ex-N&W line because the Virginian's own grade there is not mapped. The C&O 'Fast Flying Virginian' is a C&O train and not this railroad. Headways are estimates throughout.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952, Virginian pp. 500-501 (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt lines 100975-101150)

properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap, no straight-line leg: 116.7 mi drawn against 119.7 mi documented (Fowler, Norfolk Main Street 0.0 - Victoria 119.7; the Feb 1952 Guide agrees). Of the raw trace, 100.0 mi runs on ways tagged old_railway_operator=Virginian/VGN (the surviving NS 'South Branch' out of Norfolk, abandoned grade, and the Tobacco Heritage Trail on the lifted Jarratt - Alberta - Kenbridge stretch) and 13.7 mi on OSM abandoned ways named 'Virginian Railway' that carry no operator tag (Algren - Suffolk and near Jarratt). OTHER-COMPANY TRACK at Norfolk: the last 3.1 mi into the city are drawn on the Norfolk and Portsmouth Belt Line (2.5 mi, OSM 'Main Line'/'ERR Main Line') and on the N&W-tagged 'Norfolk Terminal' track across the Eastern Branch (0.6 mi) - that is the approach to the Terminal Station site that OSM maps today; that the Virginian's trains used exactly these tracks is not established. The terminal trackage itself is lifted, so the line stops about 0.8 km (0.5 mi) short of the Norfolk Terminal Station site (36.84308, -76.28194). LATER-ALIGNMENT CAVEAT: Norfolk Terminal Station opened only in 1912, so the 1907-1912 years are drawn to a terminal that did not yet exist; where Virginian passengers boarded in Norfolk before 1912 is not established. Elsewhere the drawn track is the line as last mapped; no realignment is recorded in the report.

segments.note: Norfolk - Victoria opened 17 Jun 1907 with one train each way daily except Sunday, 12 hours (first schedules in the Norfolk Virginian-Pilot, via Wikipedia, Victoria VA). This start is after the 8 Mar 1907 consolidation of the Tidewater Railway into the Virginian, so it is a Virginian train; no Tidewater-name passenger train is drawn. Ends where through service to Roanoke began in 1909. headway_min is an estimate from the train count, not a timetable reading.
sources: Segment-level: 17 Jun 1907 start from Wikipedia (Victoria, Virginia), citing the first schedules; headway from that one-train-a-day statement. Recorded in research/branches/virginian_railway.txt [1].

segments.note: Through Norfolk - Roanoke service from 1909 (regular Deepwater - Norfolk service reported inaugurated 12 Jul 1909, NH). Two trains each way - day trains and an overnight train with Pullman buffet-sleepers until 1937 per a Trains.com forum post (rcdrye), unverified. Both the 1937 era split and the 720-minute headway are estimates resting on that post, not on a timetable.
sources: NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL: the 1937 split and the two-trains-a-day frequency rest only on a forum post (rcdrye, Trains.com 2015); no timetable of these years was checked. 1909 start per research/branches/virginian_railway.txt [1]/[2].

segments.note: One train each way, Nos. 3/4: Norfolk 8:00 AM - Roanoke 4:00 PM and return (Feb 1952 Official Guide, tables dated January 1952; the 1954 SCC report gives the same). The SCC refused discontinuance on 26 Jul 1954, then allowed it by order of 11 Jan 1956 effective 29 Jan 1956, the last Virginian passenger train in Virginia. From mid-1955 the train ran with leased N&W coaches (forum, unverified). Freight continued, under the N&W after the 1 Dec 1959 merger. Headway is one train a day, counted from the 1952 schedule.
sources: Segment-level: 29 Jan 1956 end from Virginia SCC Case No. 12067, order of 11 Jan 1956 (transcribed at nwhistory.info); one train each way from the Feb 1952 Official Guide and the SCC 1954 report. The 1937 start of this era is a forum date, unverified.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap, no straight-line leg: 81.3 mi drawn against 82.7 mi documented (Fowler, Roanoke 243.1 - Hales Gap 325.8). Hales Gap has no OSM node, so the feature ends at a point measured 2.0 mi (Fowler: Glen Lyn 323.8, Hales Gap 325.8) along the line past the Glen Lyn village node; Kellysville then falls 1.85 mi further on against 2.0 documented, which supports the placement. OTHER-COMPANY TRACK, AND NOT THE VIRGINIAN'S OWN ROUTE: between Whitethorne and Ripplemead the Virginian's own grade along the New River is lifted and is mapped in neither OSM nor OpenHistoricalMap, so 15.7 mi are drawn on the parallel ex-N&W line (OSM 'Christiansburg District', old_railway_operator=N&W) through Eggleston and Pembroke, reached by a 1.7 mi untagged post-merger connection near Whitethorne. That track belongs to another company and stands in for the Virginian grade, which ran close by in the same valley (which bank, and how far, was not verified); treat this 17.4 mi as an approximation. The rest (about 64 mi) is on Virginian-tagged ways: NS's 'Whitethorne District' Roanoke - Salem - Ellett - Whitethorne, and from Ripplemead through Narrows and Glen Lyn, where the Virginian's New River bridge and the grade beside US 460 are gone (wvrails.net) but still mapped as Virginian.

segments.note: New River Division Nos. 3/4 (3-103 / 104-4 in the 1952 Guide). Regular service from 12 Jul 1909 (NH). In 1954 the train ran Roanoke 7:30 AM - Page 2:46 PM and Page 9:28 AM - Roanoke 4:35 PM (SCC report); it did not connect at Roanoke with the Norfolk train. The Virginia SCC allowed discontinuance Roanoke - Va./W.Va. state line 'on and after December 31, 1954' (order 19 Nov 1954); the forum source gives the same date for the 5 West Virginia miles to Hales Gap, unverified. The 1925 electrification changed freight motive power only - passenger trains stayed steam. Track stayed in freight use. Headway: one train each way in the 1950s (SCC, Guide); earlier there may have been two (forum) - headway_min is an estimate from the train count, not a timetable reading.
sources: Segment-level: 1909 start from NH; 31 Dec 1954 end from Virginia SCC Case No. 12067, order of 19 Nov 1954 (state line to Hales Gap, 5 mi, rests on the forum post only).
Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952, Virginian pp. 500-501 (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt lines 100975-101150)

segments.note: Through Roanoke - Princeton - Mullens - Page - Deepwater service from 1909: Princeton reached 30 May 1909 (varails.com), regular service 12 Jul 1909 (NH). Princeton was the shop and division town. The Jan 1952 tables show the train running through to D. B. Tower. Page - Mullens had carried Deepwater Railway trains in Jan 1907 (separate feature); no evidence of Virginian-name trains here Mar 1907 - Jul 1909 was found, so the Virginian era starts 1909. This end is OPEN: 1954 is the last CONFIRMED year (the 1954 Virginia SCC report describes the Roanoke - Page train then running), not a known end. A Trains.com forum post (ElmoreTRM) says a Hales Gap - Page remnant ran after 31 Dec 1954 until 11 Jul 1955; that is unverified, so 1955 is withheld. Do not extend without evidence such as a W.Va. PSC order or a Beckley/Princeton newspaper. headway_min is an estimate from the train count, not a timetable reading.
sources: Segment-level: 1909 start from varails.com and NH; 1954 is the last confirmed year, from the SCC 1954 report and the Feb 1952 Guide. The forum's 11 Jul 1955 end is unverified and withheld.

segments.note: ANCHOR: one proven year. The January 1907 Official Guide lists the stop (Fowler: 'Mullins 1/1907G'), and track reached Mullens in Nov 1906 (Mullens historical marker). The Deepwater Railway was a legally separate company until its 8 Mar 1907 consolidation into the Virginian. Service certainly ran wider than this single year both ways - from the late-1906 arrival of track, and under the Virginian name after March 1907 - but no other year is confirmed for a Deepwater Railway train here. Do not widen without evidence. Headway is a placeholder estimate; no Deepwater Railway timetable was seen.

segments.note: Until 1931 Virginian trains ended at Deepwater on the C&O, connecting there for Charleston and the west; into the early 1930s through coaches/sleepers and 'Club-Diners' were forwarded over the C&O via West Deepwater (NH; NWHS; forum). Those through cars rode C&O trains on C&O track and are not drawn here. Ends 15 Mar 1931 when the new Kanawha River bridge took the trains to D. B. Tower on the NYC (next feature). The 1909 start is the start of regular through service; Virginian trains between Mar 1907 and 1909 are plausible but unproven. headway_min is an estimate from the train count, not a timetable reading (the forum says Nos. 3/4 and 5/6 ran west of Mullens at first, i.e. two each way).
sources: Segment-level: 1909 start from NH (12 Jul 1909); the 15 Mar 1931 changeover from the forum post (ElmoreTRM), with wvrails.net and NH giving 1931 for the bridge (NWHS says 1930 - conflict recorded in metadata).

Tower at NYC mp 31.2). OTHER-COMPANY TRACK, BY DESIGN: the whole feature is drawn on the New York Central's ex-Kanawha & Michigan line on the north/east bank of the Kanawha (OSM 'Kanawha River Railroad', old_railway_operator=NYC, 31.3 of 31.3 mi), which the Virginian used under trackage rights - the trains, crews and engines were Virginian, so the feature carries Virginian colour; the track was NYC-owned. Charleston end placed on that line near the east side of downtown (38.35512, -81.62969), 0.5 mi west of where Fowler's Elizabeth Street stop would fall; the NYC/K&M Charleston station site was not pinned exactly. The drawn track is the line as last mapped.

segments.note: Virginian trains ran D. B. Tower - Charleston over the NYC under trackage rights from 15 Mar 1931 (forum; wvrails.net and NH give 1931 for the connection, NWHS says 1930 - conflict recorded, 1931 adopted). They could carry passengers only to and from Virginian points, and made no stops on the NYC (Fowler: D. B. Tower '* stops for Virginian Rly trains only'). Trains 3/4 and 5/6 at first; 5/6 dropped Mullens - Charleston in 1932 (forum). Ended 24 Jan 1952 per the forum (ElmoreTRM); rcdrye says 1951, when the NYC withdrew from the joint service. The January 1952 Guide tables end at D. B. Tower. The 24 days of 1952 are forum-only and withheld, so the drawn end is 1951. Headway 720 (two each way) fits 1931-32 only; afterwards one each way - an estimate either way.
sources: Segment-level: 15 Mar 1931 start and Jan 1952 end from the Trains.com forum (ElmoreTRM, citing employee timetables), with the year corroborated by wvrails.net and NH; the Feb 1952 Guide's table ending at D. B. Tower is used only as corroboration. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: START IS OPEN: 1911 is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known opening of passenger service - Fowler prints 1911 Official Guide tags at Hot Coal ('Patterson 1911G') and Mistletoe ('Goodwin 1911G') near Loop Junction. The branch's opening date is unknown; do not move the start earlier without evidence. Trains 13/14 ran Mullens - Fireco in Employee Time Table No. 3, 30 Nov 1919 (forum, citing the ETT). Passenger trains ended in December 1940 per the forum post (ElmoreTRM, 'The Winding Gulf passenger trains were eliminated in December 1940'), unverified.
